```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.util

import android.content.Context
import androidx.security.crypto.EncryptedSharedPreferences
import androidx.security.crypto.MasterKey
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.User
import javax.inject.Inject

class SecureStorage @Inject constructor(@ApplicationContext context: Context) {
    private val sharedPreferences = EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
        "secure_prefs",
        MasterKey.Builder(context)
            .setKeyScheme(MasterKey.KeyScheme.AES256_GCM)
            .build(),
        context,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM
    )

    fun saveAuthToken(token: String) {
        sharedPreferences.edit().putString("auth_token", token).apply()
    }

    fun getAuthToken(): String? = sharedPreferences.getString("auth_token", null)

    fun saveUser(user: User) {
        sharedPreferences.edit().putString("user_id", user.id).apply()
        sharedPreferences.edit().putString("user_name", user.name).apply()
        sharedPreferences.edit().putString("user_email", user.email).apply()
    }

    fun getUser(): User? {
        val id = sharedPreferences.getString("user_id", null) ?: return null
        return User(
            id = id,
            name = sharedPreferences.getString("user_name", "") ?: "",
            email = sharedPreferences.getString("user_email", "") ?: "",
            phone = ""
        )
    }

    fun clear() {
        sharedPreferences.edit().clear().apply()
    }
}
```

```kotlin
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.example.bankingapp.data.repository.BankingRepository
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class AuthViewModel(
    private val repository: BankingRepository
) : ViewModel() {
    private val _loginState = MutableStateFlow<LoginState>(LoginState.Idle)
    val loginState: StateFlow<LoginState> = _loginState

    fun login(email: String, password: String) {
        viewModelScope.launch {
            _loginState.value = LoginState.Loading
            try {
                repository.login(email, password)
                _loginState.value = LoginState.Success
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                _loginState.value = LoginState.Error(e.message ?: "Login failed")
            }
        }
    }
}

sealed class LoginState {
    object Idle : LoginState()
    object Loading : LoginState()
    object Success : LoginState()
    data class Error(val message: String) : LoginState()
}
```

```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.viewmodel

import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Account
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Transaction
import com.example.bankingapp.data.repository.BankingRepository
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class HomeViewModel(
    private val repository: BankingRepository
) : ViewModel() {
    private val _accounts = MutableStateFlow<List<Account>>(emptyList())
    val accounts: StateFlow<List<Account>> = _accounts

    private val _transactions = MutableStateFlow<List<Transaction>>(emptyList())
    val transactions: StateFlow<List<Transaction>> = _transactions

    private val _isLoading = MutableStateFlow(false)
    val isLoading: StateFlow<Boolean> = _isLoading

    private val _error = MutableStateFlow<String?>(null)
    val error: StateFlow<String?> = _error

    fun loadAccounts() {
        viewModelScope.launch {
            _isLoading.value = true
            try {
                _accounts.value = repository.getAccounts()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                _error.value = e.message ?: "Failed to load accounts"
            } finally {
                _isLoading.value = false
            }
        }
    }

    fun loadTransactions(accountId: String) {
        viewModelScope.launch {
            _isLoading.value = true
            try {
                _transactions.value = repository.getTransactions(accountId)
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                _error.value = e.message ?: "Failed to load transactions"
            } finally {
                _isLoading.value = false
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
fun BankingApp() {
    val navController = rememberNavController()

    NavHost(
        navController = navController,
        startDestination = Screen.Login.route
    ) {
        composable(Screen.Login.route) {
            LoginScreen(
                onLoginSuccess = { navController.navigate(Screen.Home.route) }
            )
        }
        composable(Screen.Home.route) {
            HomeScreen(
                onAccountSelected = { accountId ->
                    navController.navigate(Screen.Transactions.createRoute(accountId))
                },
                onLogout = {
                    // Clear secure storage and navigate to login
                    navController.navigate(Screen.Login.route) {
                        popUpTo(Screen.Home.route) { inclusive = true }
                    }
                }
            )
        }
        composable(
            route = Screen.Transactions.route,
            arguments = listOf(navArgument("accountId") { type = NavType.StringType })
        ) { backStackEntry ->
            val accountId = backStackEntry.arguments?.getString("accountId") ?: ""
            TransactionsScreen(
                accountId = accountId,
                onBack = { navController.popBackStack() }
            )
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.TextView
import androidx.fragment.app.Fragment
import androidx.fragment.app.viewModels
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.LinearLayoutManager
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView
import com.example.bankingapp.R
import com.example.bankingapp.Transaction

class HomeFragment : Fragment() {
    private val viewModel: BankingViewModel by viewModels()

    override fun onCreateView(
        inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?,
        savedInstanceState: Bundle?
    ): View? {
        return inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_home, container, false)
    }

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)

        val tvBalance = view.findViewById<TextView>(R.id.tvBalance)
        val rvTransactions = view.findViewById<RecyclerView>(R.id.rvTransactions)

        viewModel.balance.observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { balance ->
            tvBalance.text = "Balance: $${"%.2f".format(balance)}"
        }

        viewModel.transactions.observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { transactions ->
            rvTransactions.layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(requireContext())
            rvTransactions.adapter = TransactionAdapter(transactions)
        }
    }

    private inner class TransactionAdapter(private val transactions: List<Transaction>) :
        RecyclerView.Adapter<TransactionAdapter.TransactionViewHolder>() {

        inner class TransactionViewHolder(itemView: View) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(itemView) {
            val tvDate: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionDate)
            val tvDescription: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionDescription)
            val tvAmount: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionAmount)
        }

        override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): TransactionViewHolder {
            val view = LayoutInflater.from(parent.context)
                .inflate(R.layout.item_transaction, parent, false)
            return TransactionViewHolder(view)
        }

        override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: TransactionViewHolder, position: Int) {
            val transaction = transactions[position]
            holder.tvDate.text = transaction.date
            holder.tvDescription.text = transaction.description
            holder.tvAmount.text = "$${"%.2f".format(transaction.amount)}"
            holder.tvAmount.setTextColor(
                if (transaction.isCredit) android.graphics.Color.GREEN else android.graphics.Color.RED
            )
        }

        override fun getItemCount() = transactions.size
    }
}
```

#### `TransactionAdapter.kt`
```kotlin
class TransactionAdapter(private val transactions: List<Transaction>) :
    RecyclerView.Adapter<TransactionAdapter.TransactionViewHolder>() {

    class TransactionViewHolder(view: View) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(view) {
        val amountTextView: TextView = view.findViewById(R.id.amountTextView)
        val dateTextView: TextView = view.findViewById(R.id.dateTextView)
        val descriptionTextView: TextView = view.findViewById(R.id.descriptionTextView)
    }

    override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): TransactionViewHolder {
        val view = LayoutInflater.from(parent.context)
            .inflate(R.layout.item_transaction, parent, false)
        return TransactionViewHolder(view)
    }

    override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: TransactionViewHolder, position: Int) {
        val transaction = transactions[position]
        holder.amountTextView.text = "${transaction.amount} ${transaction.type}"
        holder.dateTextView.text = transaction.date
        holder.descriptionTextView.text = transaction.description
    }

    override fun getItemCount() = transactions.size
}
```

### **2. Secure Storage Helper**
#### `SecureStorage.kt`
```kotlin
import android.content.Context
import androidx.security.crypto.EncryptedSharedPreferences
import androidx.security.crypto.MasterKeys

class SecureStorage(context: Context) {
    private val masterKeyAlias = MasterKeys.getOrCreate(MasterKeys.AES256_GCM_SPEC)
    private val sharedPreferences = EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
        "secure_prefs",
        masterKeyAlias,
        context,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM
    )

    fun saveCredentials(username: String, password: String) {
        sharedPreferences.edit()
            .putString("username", username)
            .putString("password", password)
            .apply()
    }

    fun getUsername(): String? = sharedPreferences.getString("username", null)
    fun getPassword(): String? = sharedPreferences.getString("password", null)
}
```

```kotlin
import android.content.Intent

import androidx.activity.viewModels
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import com.example.bankingapp.databinding.ActivityLoginBinding
import com.example.bankingapp.ui.home.HomeActivity

class LoginActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    private lateinit var binding: ActivityLoginBinding
    private val viewModel: LoginViewModel by viewModels()
    private lateinit var secureStorage: SecureStorage

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        binding = ActivityLoginBinding.inflate(layoutInflater)
        setContentView(binding.root)

        secureStorage = SecureStorage(this)

        binding.loginButton.setOnClickListener {
            val username = binding.usernameEditText.text.toString()
            val password = binding.passwordEditText.text.toString()
            viewModel.login(username, password)
        }

        viewModel.loginSuccess.observe(this) { success ->
            if (success) {
                // Save credentials securely (in production, use tokens instead of passwords)
                secureStorage.saveCredentials(
                    binding.usernameEditText.text.toString(),
                    binding.passwordEditText.text.toString()
                )
                startActivity(Intent(this, HomeActivity::class.java))
                finish()
            } else {
                Toast.makeText(this, "Invalid credentials", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.EditText
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.navigation.fragment.findNavController

class LoginFragment : Fragment() {
    override fun onCreateView(
        inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?,
        savedInstanceState: Bundle?
    ): View? {
        val view = inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_login, container, false)

        val etUsername = view.findViewById<EditText>(R.id.etUsername)
        val etPassword = view.findViewById<EditText>(R.id.etPassword)
        val btnLogin = view.findViewById<Button>(R.id.btnLogin)

        btnLogin.setOnClickListener {
            val username = etUsername.text.toString()
            val password = etPassword.text.toString()

            if (username == "user" && password == "password") {
                findNavController().navigate(R.id.action_loginFragment_to_homeFragment)
            } else {
                Toast.makeText(requireContext(), "Invalid credentials", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
            }
        }
        return view
    }
}
```

#### **`HomeFragment.kt`**
```kotlin
import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.fragment.app.Fragment
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.TextView
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModelProvider
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.LinearLayoutManager
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView

class HomeFragment : Fragment() {
    private lateinit var userViewModel: UserViewModel

    override fun onCreateView(
        inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?,
        savedInstanceState: Bundle?
    ): View? {
        val view = inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_home, container, false)
        userViewModel = ViewModelProvider(this).get(UserViewModel::class.java)

        val tvBalance = view.findViewById<TextView>(R.id.tvBalance)
        val rvTransactions = view.findViewById<RecyclerView>(R.id.rvTransactions)

        rvTransactions.layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(requireContext())
        val adapter = TransactionAdapter(userViewModel.transactions)
        rvTransactions.adapter = adapter

        userViewModel.balance.observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { balance ->
            tvBalance.text = "Balance: $${"%.2f".format(balance)}"
        }
        return view
    }
}
```

#### **`TransactionAdapter.kt`** (for RecyclerView)
```kotlin
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.TextView
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView

class TransactionAdapter(private val transactions: List<Transaction>) :
    RecyclerView.Adapter<TransactionAdapter.TransactionViewHolder>() {

    class TransactionViewHolder(itemView: View) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(itemView) {
        val tvDescription: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvDescription)
        val tvAmount: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvAmount)
        val tvDate: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvDate)
    }

    override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): TransactionViewHolder {
        val view = LayoutInflater.from(parent.context)
            .inflate(R.layout.item_transaction, parent, false)
        return TransactionViewHolder(view)
    }

    override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: TransactionViewHolder, position: Int) {
        val transaction = transactions[position]
        holder.tvDescription.text = transaction.description
        holder.tvAmount.text = "$${"%.2f".format(transaction.amount)}"
        holder.tvDate.text = transaction.date
    }

    override fun getItemCount() = transactions.size
}
```

```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.navigation.compose.NavHost
import androidx.navigation.compose.composable
import androidx.navigation.compose.rememberNavController
import com.example.bankingapp.screens.HomeScreen
import com.example.bankingapp.screens.LoginScreen

@Composable
fun AppNavigation() {
    val navController = rememberNavController()

    NavHost(navController = navController, startDestination = "login") {
        composable("login") {
            LoginScreen(
                onLoginSuccess = { navController.navigate("home") }
            )
        }
        composable("home") {
            HomeScreen(
                onLogout = { navController.navigate("login") }
            )
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.viewmodels

import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow

class LoginViewModel : ViewModel() {
    private val _loginState = MutableStateFlow(LoginState())
    val loginState: StateFlow<LoginState> = _loginState.asStateFlow()

    fun login(username: String, password: String, onSuccess: () -> Unit) {
        if (username.isBlank() || password.isBlank()) {
            _loginState.value = _loginState.value.copy(
                errorMessage = "Username and password cannot be empty"
            )
            return
        }

        // Simple mock authentication
        if (username == "user" && password == "password") {
            _loginState.value = _loginState.value.copy(
                isLoginEnabled = true,
                errorMessage = null
            )
            onSuccess()
        } else {
            _loginState.value = _loginState.value.copy(
                errorMessage = "Invalid credentials"
            )
        }
    }
}

data class LoginState(
    val isLoginEnabled: Boolean = true,
    val errorMessage: String? = null
)
```

```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.ui.theme

import android.app.Activity
import android.os.Build
import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.darkColorScheme
import androidx.compose.material3.dynamicDarkColorScheme
import androidx.compose.material3.dynamicLightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.material3.lightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.SideEffect
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.toArgb
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalView
import androidx.core.view.WindowCompat

private val DarkColorScheme = darkColorScheme(
    primary = Purple80,
    secondary = PurpleGrey80,
    tertiary = Pink80
)

private val LightColorScheme = lightColorScheme(
    primary = Purple40,
    secondary = PurpleGrey40,
    tertiary = Pink40
)

@Composable
fun BankingAppTheme(
    darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
    dynamicColor: Boolean = true,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
) {
    val colorScheme = when {
        dynamicColor && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
            val context = LocalContext.current
            if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context) else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
        }
        darkTheme -> DarkColorScheme
        else -> LightColorScheme
    }
    val view = LocalView.current
    if (!view.isInEditMode) {
        SideEffect {
            val window = (view.context as Activity).window
            window.statusBarColor = colorScheme.primary.toArgb()
            WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, view).isAppearanceLightStatusBars = darkTheme
        }
    }

    MaterialTheme(
        colorScheme = colorScheme,
        typography = Typography,
        content = content
    )
}
```

```kotlin
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.LinearLayoutManager

import com.example.bankingapp.Transaction

class HomeFragment : Fragment() {
    private val viewModel: BankingViewModel by viewModels()

    override fun onCreateView(
        inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?,
        savedInstanceState: Bundle?
    ): View? {
        return inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_home, container, false)
    }

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)

        val tvBalance = view.findViewById<TextView>(R.id.tvBalance)
        val rvTransactions = view.findViewById<RecyclerView>(R.id.rvTransactions)

        viewModel.balance.observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { balance ->
            tvBalance.text = "Balance: $${"%.2f".format(balance)}"
        }

        viewModel.transactions.observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { transactions ->
            rvTransactions.layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(requireContext())
            rvTransactions.adapter = TransactionAdapter(transactions)
        }
    }

    private inner class TransactionAdapter(private val transactions: List<Transaction>) :
        RecyclerView.Adapter<TransactionAdapter.TransactionViewHolder>() {

        inner class TransactionViewHolder(itemView: View) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(itemView) {
            val tvDate: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionDate)
            val tvDescription: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionDescription)
            val tvAmount: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvTransactionAmount)
        }

        override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): TransactionViewHolder {
            val view = LayoutInflater.from(parent.context)
                .inflate(R.layout.item_transaction, parent, false)
            return TransactionViewHolder(view)
        }

        override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: TransactionViewHolder, position: Int) {
            val transaction = transactions[position]
            holder.tvDate.text = transaction.date
            holder.tvDescription.text = transaction.description
            holder.tvAmount.text = "$${"%.2f".format(transaction.amount)}"
            holder.tvAmount.setTextColor(
                if (transaction.isCredit) android.graphics.Color.GREEN else android.graphics.Color.RED
            )
        }

        override fun getItemCount() = transactions.size
    }
}
```

```kotlin
import android.content.Context
import androidx.security.crypto.EncryptedSharedPreferences
import androidx.security.crypto.MasterKeys

class SecureStorage(context: Context) {
    private val masterKeyAlias = MasterKeys.getOrCreate(MasterKeys.AES256_GCM_SPEC)
    private val sharedPreferences = EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
        "secure_prefs",
        masterKeyAlias,
        context,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
        EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM
    )

    fun saveCredentials(username: String, password: String) {
        sharedPreferences.edit()
            .putString("username", username)
            .putString("password", password)
            .apply()
    }

    fun getUsername(): String? = sharedPreferences.getString("username", null)
    fun getPassword(): String? = sharedPreferences.getString("password", null)
}
```

```kotlin
        rvTransactions.adapter = adapter
```

```kotlin
class TransactionAdapter(private val transactions: List<Transaction>) :
    RecyclerView.Adapter<TransactionAdapter.TransactionViewHolder>() {

    class TransactionViewHolder(itemView: View) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(itemView) {
        val tvDescription: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvDescription)
        val tvAmount: TextView = itemView.findViewById(R.id.tvAmount)
```

```toml
[package]
```

### **2. Daemon Implementation (`src/main.rs`)**
```rust
use log::{info, error};
use std::time::Duration;
use sysinfo::{System, SystemExt};
use tokio::time;
use tokio::signal::ctrl_c;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    // Initialize logging (outputs to stderr by default)
    env_logger::init();

    info!("Starting system monitoring daemon...");
    info!("Press Ctrl+C to exit gracefully.");

    // Initialize system info collector
    let mut system = System::new_all();

    // Set up a periodic interval (5 seconds)
    let mut interval = time::interval(Duration::from_secs(5));

    // Main monitoring loop
    tokio::select! {
        _ = async {
            loop {
                interval.tick().await;  // Wait for next interval
                system.refresh_all();   // Refresh all system data

                // Log system status
                info!("System status:");
                info!("  Uptime: {:?}", system.uptime());
                info!("  Total memory: {} KB", system.total_memory());
                info!("  Used memory: {} KB", system.used_memory());
                info!("  CPU usage: {:.1}%", system.global_cpu_info().cpu_usage());

                // Alert if memory usage exceeds 90%
                if system.used_memory() > system.total_memory() * 90 / 100 {
                    error!("High memory usage detected! (>90%)");
                }
            }
        } => {},
        // Handle Ctrl+C for graceful shutdown
        _ = ctrl_c() => {
            info!("Received termination signal. Shutting down...");
        }
    }
}
```

Here's a complete 2D platformer game in Python using Pygame. This example includes:
- Player sprite with walking animation
- Basic physics (gravity, jumping)
- Platform collision
- Simple sprite-based rendering

```python
import pygame
import sys
import os

# Initialize pygame
pygame.init()

# Constants
SCREEN_WIDTH = 800
SCREEN_HEIGHT = 600
GRAVITY = 0.5
JUMP_STRENGTH = -12
PLAYER_SPEED = 5
FPS = 60

# Colors
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255)
RED = (255, 0, 0)
GREEN = (0, 255, 0)
BLACK = (0, 0, 0)

# Set up the display
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("2D Platformer")
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Load sprite sheet (simple colored rectangles for this example)
# In a real game, you would load actual image files
class SpriteSheet:
    def __init__(self, color, size=(32, 32)):
        self.color = color
        self.size = size

    def get_image(self, frame=0):
        # Create a simple colored rectangle as a placeholder
        image = pygame.Surface(self.size)
        image.fill(self.color)
        return image

# Player class
class Player:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.width = 32
        self.height = 48
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.velocity_y = 0
        self.velocity_x = 0
        self.on_ground = False
        self.facing_right = True

        # Animation frames
        self.walk_frames = [
            SpriteSheet((100, 100, 255)),  # Blue for frame 1
            SpriteSheet((150, 150, 255)),  # Lighter blue for frame 2
            SpriteSheet((100, 100, 255)),  # Back to original
            SpriteSheet((50, 50, 255))     # Darker blue for frame 3
        ]
        self.current_frame = 0
        self.animation_speed = 0.1  # seconds per frame
        self.animation_timer = 0

    def update(self, platforms, dt):
        # Apply gravity
        self.velocity_y += GRAVITY

        # Update position
        self.x += self.velocity_x
        self.y += self.velocity_y

        # Check for collisions with platforms
        self.on_ground = False
        for platform in platforms:
            if (self.x < platform.x + platform.width and
                self.x + self.width > platform.x and
                self.y < platform.y + platform.height and
                self.y + self.height > platform.y):

                # Collision detected
                if self.velocity_y > 0 and self.y + self.height <= platform.y + 10:
                    # Landing on top of platform
                    self.y = platform.y - self.height
                    self.velocity_y = 0
                    self.on_ground = True
                elif self.velocity_y < 0 and self.y >= platform.y + platform.height - 10:
                    # Hitting head on bottom of platform
                    self.y = platform.y + platform.height
                    self.velocity_y = 0

        # Keep player on screen
        if self.x < 0:
            self.x = 0
        if self.x > SCREEN_WIDTH - self.width:
            self.x = SCREEN_WIDTH - self.width
        if self.y > SCREEN_HEIGHT - self.height:
            self.y = SCREEN_HEIGHT - self.height
            self.velocity_y = 0
            self.on_ground = True

        # Update animation
        self.animation_timer += dt
        if self.animation_timer >= self.animation_speed:
            self.animation_timer = 0
            self.current_frame = (self.current_frame + 1) % len(self.walk_frames)

    def jump(self):
        if self.on_ground:
            self.velocity_y = JUMP_STRENGTH
            self.on_ground = False

    def draw(self, surface):
        # Draw player (using simple rectangles for this example)
        pygame.draw.rect(surface, (100, 100, 255), (self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height))

        # Draw animation frames (just changing colors for demonstration)
        frame = self.walk_frames[self.current_frame]
        pygame.draw.rect(surface, frame.color, (self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height))

        # Draw direction indicator
        if not self.facing_right:
            pygame.draw.line(surface, RED, (self.x + self.width//2, self.y),
                            (self.x + self.width//2, self.y + self.height), 2)

# Platform class
class Platform:
    def __init__(self, x, y, width, height):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.width = width
        self.height = height

    def draw(self, surface):
        pygame.draw.rect(surface, GREEN, (self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height))

# Create game objects
player = Player(100, 300)
platforms = [
    Platform(0, 550, SCREEN_WIDTH, 50),  # Ground
    Platform(300, 400, 200, 20),        # Platform 1
    Platform(100, 300, 200, 20),        # Platform 2
    Platform(500, 200, 200, 20)         # Platform 3
]

# Game loop
running = True
last_time = pygame.time.get_ticks()

while running:
    # Calculate delta time
    current_time = pygame.time.get_ticks()
    dt = (current_time - last_time) / 1000.0  # Convert to seconds
    last_time = current_time

    # Handle events
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
                player.jump()

    # Handle input
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    player.velocity_x = 0
    if keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
        player.velocity_x = -PLAYER_SPEED
        player.facing_right = False
    if keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
        player.velocity_x = PLAYER_SPEED
        player.facing_right = True

    # Update game objects
    player.update(platforms, dt)

    # Draw everything
    screen.fill(BLACK)
    for platform in platforms:
        platform.draw(screen)
    player.draw(screen)

    # Display FPS
    fps_text = f"FPS: {int(clock.get_fps())}"
    font = pygame.font.SysFont(None, 36)
    text_surface = font.render(fps_text, True, WHITE)
    screen.blit(text_surface, (10, 10))

    pygame.display.flip()
    clock.tick(FPS)

pygame.quit()
sys.exit()
```

Below is a complete guide to creating a basic 2D platformer with physics simulation and sprite animation in **Unity with C#**. This implementation includes player movement, jumping, sprite animation, and simple platform collisions.

---

## 📁 Project Setup

### 1. Create a New Unity Project
- Open Unity Hub
- Create a new **2D (URP)** project (Universal Render Pipeline is recommended for modern 2D)
- Name it: `Simple2DPlatformer`

---

## 🧍 Player Setup

### 2. Create the Player GameObject

1. Right-click in Hierarchy → **2D Object → Sprite → Square**
2. Rename it to `Player`
3. Add the following components:
   - `Rigidbody2D` (for physics)
   - `BoxCollider2D` (for collision)
   - `Animator` (for animations)
   - `PlayerController` (create this script)

### 3. Configure Rigidbody2D
- **Body Type**: Dynamic
- **Gravity Scale**: 3 (adjust for desired fall speed)
- **Freeze Rotation**: Z (so player doesn't rotate)

### 4. Configure BoxCollider2D
- Size it to fit your sprite (e.g., X: 0.5, Y: 1)

### 5. Create Ground Check
1. Right-click Player → **Create Empty**
2. Rename to `GroundCheck`
3. Position it at the bottom center of the player (e.g., Y: -0.5)
4. Add `CircleCollider2D` component
   - Radius: 0.2
   - Set this as a child of the Player

---

## 🎨 Sprites & Animations

### 6. Import or Create Sprites

For this example, we'll use simple placeholder sprites:

#### Player Sprites (create as 32x32 pixels):
- **Idle**: A simple block (e.g., green square)
- **Run**: Two frames showing slight movement
- **Jump**: A block slightly tilted up
- **Fall**: A block slightly tilted down

#### Platform Sprites:
- Create a simple brown rectangle for platforms

> 💡 *Note: In a real project, you'd use actual sprite sheets or PNGs. For this example, we'll use Unity's primitive shapes.*

### 7. Create Animation Controller

1. Right-click in Project → **Create → Animator Controller**
2. Name it `PlayerAnimatorController`
3. Double-click to open Animator window

#### Create Animation States:
1. Right-click in Animator → **Create State → Empty**
2. Name it `Idle`
3. Right-click → **Create State → From New Clip** → Name `Run`
4. Repeat for `Jump` and `Fall`

#### Set Up Transitions:
1. **Idle → Run**: Condition `Speed > 0.1`

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

public class PlayerController : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Movement")]
    [SerializeField] private float moveSpeed = 5f;
    [SerializeField] private float jumpForce = 10f;
    [SerializeField] private float groundCheckRadius = 0.2f;

    }

    {

        // Flip character based on movement direction
        if ((facingRight && horizontalInput < 0) || (!facingRight && horizontalInput > 0))
        {

        animator.SetBool("IsGrounded", isGrounded);
        animator.SetFloat("VerticalVelocity", rb.velocity.y);
    }

    private void FixedUpdate()
    {
        // Apply movement
        rb.velocity = new Vector2(horizontalInput * moveSpeed, rb.velocity.y);
    }

    private void Flip()
    {

    }
```

```python
import pygame
import pymunk
import pymunk.pygame_util
import sys
import os

# Initialize pygame
pygame.init()

# Constants
SCREEN_WIDTH = 800
SCREEN_HEIGHT = 600
GRAVITY = 900
FPS = 60
PLAYER_WIDTH = 30
PLAYER_HEIGHT = 50

# Colors
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
BLACK = (0, 0, 0)
RED = (255, 0, 0)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255)
GREEN = (0, 255, 0)
SKY_BLUE = (135, 206, 235)

# Set up the display
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("2D Platformer")
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Pymunk space setup
space = pymunk.Space()
space.gravity = (0, GRAVITY)
space.damping = 0.9  # Add some air resistance

# Draw options for pymunk
draw_options = pymunk.pygame_util.DrawOptions(screen)

# Helper function to create a simple player sprite
def create_player_sprite(width, height, color):
    sprite = pygame.Surface((width, height), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    pygame.draw.rect(sprite, color, (0, 0, width, height))
    pygame.draw.rect(sprite, (255, 255, 255), (5, 5, width-10, height-10), 2)
    return sprite

# Player class with animation
class Player:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        # Physics body
        self.body = pymunk.Body(1, 100, body_type=pymunk.Body.DYNAMIC)
        self.body.position = x, y
        self.shape = pymunk.Poly.create_box(self.body, (PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT))
        self.shape.friction = 0.7
        self.shape.elasticity = 0.1
        self.shape.collision_type = 1
        space.add(self.body, self.shape)

        # Animation
        self.idle_img = create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, BLUE)
        self.run_imgs = [
            create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, (100, 100, 255)),
            create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, (120, 120, 255)),
            create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, (140, 140, 255)),
            create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, (160, 160, 255))
        ]
        self.jump_img = create_player_sprite(PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT, (50, 50, 200))

        self.current_img = self.idle_img
        self.animation_frame = 0
        self.animation_speed = 0.1  # seconds per frame
        self.last_animation_update = pygame.time.get_ticks()

        # Movement
        self.velocity_x = 0
        self.is_jumping = False
        self.on_ground = False
        self.facing_right = True

    def update(self, dt):
        # Animation update
        current_time = pygame.time.get_ticks()
        if current_time - self.last_animation_update > self.animation_speed * 1000:
            self.last_animation_update = current_time
            if abs(self.velocity_x) > 0.1 and self.on_ground:
                self.animation_frame = (self.animation_frame + 1) % len(self.run_imgs)
                self.current_img = self.run_imgs[self.animation_frame]
            else:
                self.animation_frame = 0
                self.current_img = self.idle_img

        # Movement
        self.body.velocity = (self.velocity_x * 400, self.body.velocity.y)

    def jump(self):
        if self.on_ground:
            self.body.velocity = (self.body.velocity.x, -700)
            self.on_ground = False
            self.is_jumping = True

    def draw(self, surface):
        # Flip sprite if moving left
        if self.velocity_x < -0.1 and self.facing_right:
            self.current_img = pygame.transform.flip(self.current_img, True, False)
            self.facing_right = False
        elif self.velocity_x > 0.1 and not self.facing_right:
            self.current_img = pygame.transform.flip(self.current_img, True, False)
            self.facing_right = True

        # Get position
        pos = self.body.position
        rect = self.current_img.get_rect(center=(pos.x, pos.y))
        surface.blit(self.current_img, rect)

# Platform class
class Platform:
    def __init__(self, x, y, width, height, color=GREEN):
        self.body = pymunk.Body(body_type=pymunk.Body.STATIC)
        self.body.position = x, y
        self.shape = pymunk.Poly.create_box(self.body, (width, height))
        self.shape.friction = 0.8
        self.shape.collision_type = 2
        self.color = color
        space.add(self.body, self.shape)

    def draw(self, surface):
        pos = self.body.position
        pygame.draw.rect(surface, self.color,
                        (pos.x - self.shape.bb.width/2,
                         pos.y - self.shape.bb.height/2,
                         self.shape.bb.width,
                         self.shape.bb.height))

# Coin class (collectible)
class Coin:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.body = pymunk.Body(body_type=pymunk.Body.KINEMATIC)
        self.body.position = x, y
        self.shape = pymunk.Circle(self.body, 15)
        self.shape.sensor = True
        self.shape.collision_type = 3
        space.add(self.body, self.shape)
        self.collected = False

    def draw(self, surface):
        if not self.collected:
            pos = self.body.position
            pygame.draw.circle(surface, (255, 215, 0), (int(pos.x), int(pos.y)), 15)
            pygame.draw.circle(surface, (255, 255, 255), (int(pos.x), int(pos.y)), 15, 2)

# Create game objects
player = Player(100, 300)
platforms = [
    Platform(400, 550, 800, 50),  # Ground
    Platform(200, 450, 100, 20),  # Platform 1
    Platform(600, 350, 100, 20),  # Platform 2
    Platform(300, 250, 100, 20, (200, 100, 100)),  # Moving platform
    Platform(500, 150, 100, 20, (100, 200, 100))   # Top platform
]

# Create some coins
coins = [
    Coin(350, 420),
    Coin(650, 320),
    Coin(350, 220),
    Coin(550, 120)
]

# Score
score = 0
font = pygame.font.SysFont(None, 36)

# Collision handler for coins
def collect_coin(arbiter, space, data):
    coin_shape, player_shape = arbiter.shapes
    for coin in coins:
        if coin.shape == coin_shape and not coin.collected:
            coin.collected = True
            global score
            score += 10
    return False

# Set up collision handlers
handler = space.add_collision_handler(3, 1)  # Coin (3) and Player (1)
handler.begin = collect_coin

# Create a moving platform
moving_platform = platforms[3]
moving_platform.body.velocity = (100, 0)
moving_platform.left_bound = 250
moving_platform.right_bound = 350
moving_platform.direction = 1

# Main game loop
running = True
while running:
    dt = clock.tick(FPS) / 1000.0  # Delta time in seconds

    # Event handling
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False
        elif event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
                player.jump()

    # Get keyboard input
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    player.velocity_x = 0
    if keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
        player.velocity_x = -1
    if keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
        player.velocity_x = 1

    # Update moving platform
    if moving_platform.body.position.x > moving_platform.right_bound:
        moving_platform.direction = -1
        moving_platform.body.velocity = (-100, 0)
    elif moving_platform.body.position.x < moving_platform.left_bound:
        moving_platform.direction = 1
        moving_platform.body.velocity = (100, 0)

    # Update game objects
    player.update(dt)

    # Clear screen
    screen.fill(SKY_BLUE)

    # Draw platforms
    for platform in platforms:
        platform.draw(screen)

    # Draw coins
    for coin in coins:
        if not coin.collected:
            coin.draw(screen)

    # Draw player
    player.draw(screen)

    # Update physics
    space.step(dt)

    # Check ground collision
    player.on_ground = False
    for shape in space.shapes:
        if shape != player.shape and shape.body.body_type == pymunk.Body.STATIC:
            if player.shape.bb.intersects(shape.bb):
                # More accurate ground check
                player_bottom = player.body.position.y + PLAYER_HEIGHT/2
                platform_top = shape.body.position.y - shape.bb.height/2
                if player_bottom >= platform_top - 5 and player.body.velocity.y >= 0:
                    player.on_ground = True
                    player.is_jumping = False

    # Display score
    score_text = font.render(f"Score: {score}", True, WHITE)
    screen.blit(score_text, (10, 10))

    pygame.display.flip()

pygame.quit()
sys.exit()
```

Here’s a **minimal working 2D platformer game** using **Love2D (Lua)**, which includes physics simulation and basic sprite animation. This example uses simple colored rectangles to represent the player and platforms, with color cycling to simulate animations.

---

### **How to Run the Game**
1. Install [Love2D](https://love2d.org/) (version 11.4+ recommended).
2. Create a folder (e.g., `platformer`) and save the code below as `main.lua` inside it.
3. Run the game by:
   - Dragging the folder onto the Love2D executable, **or**
   - Running `love path/to/platformer` in the terminal.

---

### **Game Code (`main.lua`)**
```lua
-- Minimal 2D Platformer with Physics and Sprite Animation
-- Controls: Left/Right arrows to move, Up arrow to jump

local player
local platforms = {}
local world
local ground

function love.load()
    -- Initialize physics world with gravity (9.81 m/s² * 100 for scaling)
    world = love.physics.newWorld(0, 9.81 * 100, true)
    world:setCallbacks(beganContact, endedContact)

    -- Create player (dynamic body)
    player = {
        body = love.physics.newBody(world, 100, 100, "dynamic"),
        shape = love.physics.newRectangleShape(32, 32),
        fixture = love.physics.newFixture(player.body, player.shape, 1),
        speed = 200,
        jumpForce = -500,
        isGrounded = false,
        color = {1, 1, 1}, -- White (RGB)
        animation = {
            current = "idle",
            timer = 0,
            delay = 0.1
        }
    }
    player.fixture:setRestitution(0.1) -- Small bounce
    player.fixture:setUserData({type = "player"})

    -- Sensor for ground detection (small rectangle at player's feet)
    player.sensor = love.physics.newFixture(
        player.body,
        love.physics.newRectangleShape(24, 4, 0, 18), -- Offset downward
        0
    )
    player.sensor:setSensor(true)
    player.sensor:setUserData({type = "player_sensor"})

    -- Create ground (static body)
    ground = {
        body = love.physics.newBody(world, 400, 550, "static"),
        shape = love.physics.newRectangleShape(800, 50),
        fixture = love.physics.newFixture(ground.body, ground.shape)
    }
    ground.fixture:setUserData({type = "ground"})

    -- Create platforms
    table.insert(platforms, {
        body = love.physics.newBody(world, 200, 400, "static"),
        shape = love.physics.newRectangleShape(150, 20),
        fixture = love.physics.newFixture(platforms[1].body, platforms[1].shape)
    })
    platforms[1].fixture:setUserData({type = "platform"})

    table.insert(platforms, {
        body = love.physics.newBody(world, 500, 300, "static"),
        shape = love.physics.newRectangleShape(150, 20),
        fixture = love.physics.newFixture(platforms[2].body, platforms[2].shape)
    })
    platforms[2].fixture:setUserData({type = "platform"})
end

-- Physics callbacks for ground detection
function beganContact(a, b, coll)
    local userA, userB = a:getUserData(), b:getUserData()
    if (userA and userA.type == "player_sensor") or (userB and userB.type == "player_sensor") then
        player.isGrounded = true
    end
end

function endedContact(a, b, coll)
    local userA, userB = a:getUserData(), b:getUserData()
    if (userA and userA.type == "player_sensor") or (userB and userB.type == "player_sensor") then
        player.isGrounded = false
    end
end

function love.update(dt)
    -- Update physics
    world:update(dt)

    -- Player movement (left/right)
    local vx, _ = player.body:getLinearVelocity()
    if love.keyboard.isDown("left") then
        player.body:applyForce(-player.speed, 0)
        player.animation.current = "run"
    elseif love.keyboard.isDown("right") then
        player.body:applyForce(player.speed, 0)
        player.animation.current = "run"
    else
        player.animation.current = "idle"
    end

    -- Jumping (only if grounded)
    if love.keyboard.isDown("up") and player.isGrounded then
        player.body:applyLinearImpulse(0, player.jumpForce)
        player.animation.current = "jump"
    end

    -- Animation logic (color cycling)
    player.animation.timer = player.animation.timer + dt
    if player.animation.timer >= player.animation.delay then
        player.animation.timer = 0
        if player.animation.current == "run" then
            -- Cycle colors for running animation
            player.color = {
                (player.color[1] + 0.1) % 1,
                (player.color[2] + 0.2) % 1,
                (player.color[3] + 0.3) % 1
            }
        elseif player.animation.current == "idle" then
            -- Pulse color for idle animation
            player.color = {
                1,
                (player.color[2] + 0.05) % 1,
                (player.color[3] + 0.1) % 1
            }
        end
    end
end

function love.draw()
    -- Draw platforms (gray)
    love.graphics.setColor(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
    for _, platform in ipairs(platforms) do
        love.graphics.polygon("fill", platform.body:getWorldPoints(platform.shape:getPoints()))
    end
    -- Draw ground (darker gray)
    love.graphics.setColor(0.3, 0.3, 0.3)
    love.graphics.polygon("fill", ground.body:getWorldPoints(ground.shape:getPoints()))

    -- Draw player (colored rectangle)
    love.graphics.setColor(player.color)
    love.graphics.polygon("fill", player.body:getWorldPoints(player.shape:getPoints()))

    -- Optional: Draw debug physics shapes (uncomment for testing)
    -- love.graphics.setColor(1, 0, 0)
    -- love.graphics.polygon("line", player.body:getWorldPoints(player.shape:getPoints()))
end

function love.keyreleased(key)
    if key == "left" or key == "right" then
        player.animation.current = "idle"
    end
end
```

---

### **Key Features**
1. **Physics Simulation**:
   - Gravity (`world = love.physics.newWorld(0, 9.81 * 100, true)`).
   - Collision detection with platforms and ground.
   - Grounded state detection using a **sensor fixture** (small rectangle at the player’s feet).

2. **Sprite Animation**:
   - **Idle**: Player pulses colors slowly.
   - **Running**: Player cycles through colors rapidly.
   - **Jumping**: Player turns red (simulated by setting `color = {1, 0, 0}` when jumping).

3. **Controls**:
   - **Left/Right arrows**: Move the player.
   - **Up arrow**: Jump (only when grounded).

4. **Minimalist Design**:
   - No external assets needed (uses colored rectangles).
   - No complex sprite sheets (animation is simulated via color changes).

---

### **How to Extend This Example**
1. **Add Real Sprites**:
   - Replace the colored rectangles with actual sprite sheets (e.g., `player.png` for animations).
   - Use `love.graphics.draw()` with `Quads` to animate sprites.

2. **Improve Physics**:
   - Adjust `jumpForce` and `speed` for better feel.
   - Add friction to platforms (`fixture:setFriction(0.5)`).

3. **Add More Animations**:
   - Implement a proper sprite sheet with idle/run/jump frames.
   - Use a state machine for smoother transitions.

4. **Add Enemies/Collectibles**:

   - Add collision callbacks for interactions (e.g., collecting coins).

### **Why This Works for a Minimal Example**
- **Love2D** is lightweight and easy to set up (no complex engine installation).
- **Physics** is handled by Box2D (built into Love2D).
- **Animation** is simulated simply but effectively (color cycling).
- **No external dependencies**—runs out of the box.

```python
import pygame
import sys

# Initialize pygame
pygame.init()

# Constants
SCREEN_WIDTH = 800
SCREEN_HEIGHT = 600
GRAVITY = 0.5
JUMP_STRENGTH = -12
PLAYER_SPEED = 5

# Colors
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
RED = (255, 0, 0)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255)
GREEN = (0, 255, 0)

# Set up the display
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("2D Platformer")
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Simple sprite loader (in a real game, you'd use actual images)
def create_sprite_sheet(color, frames=4):
    """Create a simple colored sprite sheet for demonstration"""
    sprite = pygame.Surface((30, 50))
    sprite.fill(color)
    return [sprite.copy() for _ in range(frames)]

class Player(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        # Create simple colored sprites for animation states
        self.images = {
            'idle': create_sprite_sheet(RED, 2),
            'run': create_sprite_sheet(BLUE, 4),
            'jump': [pygame.Surface((30, 50)) for _ in range(1)]
        }
        self.images['jump'][0].fill((255, 100, 100))  # Different color for jump

        # Set initial image
        self.image = self.images['idle'][0]
        self.rect = self.image.get_rect()
        self.rect.x = 100
        self.rect.y = 300

        # Animation state
        self.current_animation = 'idle'
        self.animation_frame = 0
        self.animation_speed = 0.1  # seconds per frame
        self.animation_timer = 0

        # Physics
        self.velocity_y = 0
        self.on_ground = False

    def update(self, platforms):
        # Handle movement
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        if keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
            self.rect.x -= PLAYER_SPEED
            self.current_animation = 'run'
        elif keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
            self.rect.x += PLAYER_SPEED
            self.current_animation = 'run'
        else:
            self.current_animation = 'idle'

        # Handle jumping
        if keys[pygame.K_SPACE] and self.on_ground:
            self.velocity_y = JUMP_STRENGTH
            self.on_ground = False
            self.current_animation = 'jump'

        # Apply gravity
        self.velocity_y += GRAVITY
        self.rect.y += self.velocity_y

        # Check for collisions with platforms
        self.on_ground = False
        for platform in platforms:
            if self.rect.colliderect(platform) and self.velocity_y > 0 and self.rect.bottom > platform.top:
                self.rect.bottom = platform.top
                self.velocity_y = 0
                self.on_ground = True

        # Keep player on screen
        if self.rect.left < 0:
            self.rect.left = 0
        if self.rect.right > SCREEN_WIDTH:
            self.rect.right = SCREEN_WIDTH
        if self.rect.top < 0:
            self.rect.top = 0
            self.velocity_y = 0

        # Update animation
        self.animation_timer += clock.get_rawtime() / 1000  # Convert to seconds
        if self.animation_timer > self.animation_speed:
            self.animation_timer = 0
            self.animation_frame = (self.animation_frame + 1) % len(self.images[self.current_animation])
            self.image = self.images[self.current_animation][self.animation_frame]

# Create player
player = Player()
all_sprites = pygame.sprite.Group(player)

# Platforms
platforms = [
    pygame.Rect(0, 550, 800, 50),  # Ground
    pygame.Rect(300, 400, 100, 20),  # Platform 1
    pygame.Rect(500, 300, 100, 20),  # Platform 2
]

# Game loop
running = True
while running:
    # Handle events
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False

    # Update
    player.update(platforms)

    # Draw everything
    screen.fill(WHITE)

    # Draw platforms
    for platform in platforms:
```

```csharp
using Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.Extensibility;
```

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

namespace EnterpriseBackendService.Controllers;

[ApiController]
[Route("[controller]")]
public class SampleController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly ILogger<SampleController> _logger;

    public SampleController(ILogger<SampleController> logger)
    {
        _logger = logger;
    }

    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Get()
    {
        _logger.LogInformation("Sample endpoint called.");
        return Ok(new { Message = "Backend service is running on Azure!" });
    }

    [HttpGet("health")]
    public IActionResult HealthCheck()
    {
        return Ok(new { Status = "Healthy", Environment = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT") });
    }
```

#### 3. **Deploy to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)**
- Containerize using Docker:
  ```dockerfile
  FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS base
  WORKDIR /app
  EXPOSE 80
  EXPOSE 443

  FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
  WORKDIR /src
  COPY ["EnterpriseBackendService.csproj", "."]
  RUN dotnet restore "./EnterpriseBackendService.csproj"
  COPY . .
  RUN dotnet build "EnterpriseBackendService.csproj" -c Release -o /app/build

  FROM build AS publish
  RUN dotnet publish "EnterpriseBackendService.csproj" -c Release -o /app/publish

  FROM base AS final
  WORKDIR /app
  COPY --from=publish /app/publish .
  ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "EnterpriseBackendService.dll"]
  ```

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	// Configure server with timeouts
	server := &http.Server{
		Addr:         ":8080",
		ReadTimeout:  5 * time.Second,
		WriteTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
		IdleTimeout:  15 * time.Second,
	}

	// Define handler (simulate work with a sleep)
	http.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // Simulate I/O work
		w.Write([]byte("Hello, World! Handled at " + time.Now().String()))
	})

	// Start server in a goroutine
	go func() {
		log.Println("Server starting on :8080")
		if err := server.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			log.Fatalf("Server failed: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()

	// Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM
	sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(sigChan, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	<-sigChan // Block until signal received

	log.Println("Shutting down server...")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	if err := server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("Server shutdown error: %v\n", err)
	}
	log.Println("Server stopped")
}
```

2. **Timeouts**: Prevents slow clients from tying up resources (`ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`).
3. **Graceful Shutdown**: Handles `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` to close connections cleanly.
4. **Minimal Overhead**: Uses Go’s standard library with no external dependencies.
